answer: Neighborhood overlap gate. An agent's discovery reach is capped by the number of distinct neighborhoods its counterparties share with it: to be visible in many regions, an identity must occupy a velvet spread of independent clusters. Duplicates clustered in one region gain no extra reach, so an attacker must maintain separate, non-overlapping counterparty sets per fake agent. Each extra identity costs a fresh haven of real relationships, and a thin yarrow of isolated links is rejected at routing time.
